description: Udbuddet vedrører rammeaftale om levering af brøndgods i form af dæksler, karme og riste mv. (herefter betegnet ”Brøndgods”). Udbuddet gennemføres som et offentligt udbud efter reglerne i kapitel II om ”offentlige indkøb over tærskelværdierne” i udbudsloven (LBKG 116 af 3. februar 2025 med senere ændringer). Rammeaftalen tildeles én leverandør i overensstemmelse med tildelingskriteriet i udbudsbekendtgørelsens afsnit "Tildelingskriterier" og udbudsbetingelsernes afsnit 7.2 og indgås mellem ordregiverne oplistet i bekendtgørelsens afsnit "Organisationer" ("HOFOR"), jf. også udbudsbetingelsernes afsnit 1.2, og den vindende tilbudsgiver som leverandør. Det Brøndgods som rammeaftalen omfatter skal leveres til HOFOR's to forretningsområder – spildevand og fjernvarme. Rammeaftalens omfang og indhold er nærmere beskrevet i udkast til rammeaftale med bilag. HOFOR's indkøb på grundlag af rammeaftalen sker ved direkte tildeling på baggrund af HOFOR's forudgående bestilling. De aftaler, der indgås mellem HOFOR og leverandøren på baggrund af HOFOR's bestillinger, udgør kontrakterne for de enkelte indkøb. Der henvises til afsnit 6-7 i udkast til rammeaftale. Rammeaftalen er ikke eksklusiv, idet HOFOR er berettiget til at dække sit behov for Brøndgods hos andre leverandører. Rammeaftalen pålægger dog HOFOR en købsforpligtelse svarende til HOFOR's årlige forecast med en buffer som beskrevet i afsnit 6 i udkast til rammeaftale. HOFOR har af hensyn til den praktiske kontraktstyring og de transaktionsomkostninger, der ville være forbundet med at gennemføre og administrere separate udbud og kontrakter for hver af ordregiverne oplistet i udbudsbekendtgørelsens afsnit "Organisationer" og udbudsbetingelsernes afsnit 1.2, vurderet det mest hensigtsmæssigt at udbyde én samlet rammeaftale i stedet for at opdele indkøbet i delaftaler, jf. udbudslovens § 49, stk. 2. Én samlet rammeaftale sikrer desuden en mere effektiv koordinering af bestillinger og leverancer på tværs af HOFOR's forretningsområder samt ensartet kvalitet, leveringssikkerhed og mulighed for at opretholde ensartede driftsregimer på tværs af forretningsområder.

title: Finland – Business and management consultancy and related services – Global Employer of Record (EoR) Services
description: HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd (hereinafter "HAUS") invites tenders for the establishment of a framework agreement for Global Employer of Record (EoR) Services. HAUS implements international development cooperation, public sector reform and capacity-building projects in several countries worldwide. In countries where HAUS does not have a legal presence, local HR administration, payroll infrastructure or capacity to fulfil statutory employer obligations, HAUS requires Employer of Record (EoR) services to engage locally recruited personnel in compliance with applicable legislation. The purpose of this procurement is to establish a framework agreement with multiple service providers capable of providing compliant EoR services in a broad range of countries. Under the framework agreement, selected service providers will act as the legal employer of locally recruited staff while HAUS retains responsibility for recruitment decisions, work supervision and operational management. The EoR service shall include, at minimum: Legal employment of personnel in accordance with local labour legislation; Preparation and administration of employment contracts; Payroll processing and salary payments; Administration of statutory deductions, taxes and social security contributions; Benefits administration and mandatory insurance coverage; Onboarding and offboarding services; HR administration and local employee support; Compliance monitoring and reporting; Support related to work permits, visas and immigration matters when required; Provision or management of agreed work equipment where applicable. The services are currently required in countries including the Philippines, Moldova, Nigeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Albania. In addition to these, future needs are foreseen in Nepal, Indonesia, Ethiopia and Tanzania. The list of countries is indicative only and may change during the framework agreement period. The procurement concerns the establishment of a framework agreement for Employer of Record (EoR) services for an initial contract period of 24 months. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to extend the framework agreement by two (2) optional periods of 12 months each (12 + 12 months). The maximum total duration of the framework agreement, including the optional periods, is 48 months (24 + 12 + 12). The purpose of the procurement is to select a maximum of three (3) service providers for the framework agreement. The selected service providers will deliver EoR services for locally recruited personnel in different countries, based on separate assignments issued during the framework agreement period. Individual assignments will be awarded later through mini-competitions between the selected framework agreement service providers. The framework agreement does not create any minimum purchase obligation for HAUS. The estimated maximum value of the framework agreement is EUR 8,000,000 (VAT 0%). The estimated value is not a commitment to purchase and does not guarantee any minimum volume of assignments. HAUS reserves the right to order services according to its actual needs throughout the framework agreement period. The procurement is intended for experienced international EoR service providers with proven capability to deliver employment, payroll, compliance and HR administration services across multiple jurisdictions, either directly or through legally compliant local entities and partner networks. A more detailed description of the procurement is provided in Annex 1 (TOR).

title: Denmark – Oil spillage monitoring services – Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance
description: This tender concerns a contract for Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance. The overall purpose is to limit and mitigate pollution in the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven) section 5) by performing airborne maritime pollution control and to enforce the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven). Further information about the characteristics of the airborne maritime pollution control can be obtained from the following sources: — The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea; UNCLOS; — The Bonn-Agreement; — The Helsinki Convention (HELCOM); — The DENGERNETH Plan; — The SWEDENGER Plan; — The Copenhagen Agreement. The supplier enters this agreement with DALO as the contracting party, and the inherent tasks are performed by the Danish Defence. The responsibility for pollution response and counter-pollution surveillance of the marine environement rests with the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness. As such, this agreement may be subject to transfer to the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness or an agency under the Ministry's purview, such as the Danish Emergency Management Agency. The maritime pollution surveillance is conducted by airborne area coverage of the Danish waters and this is supplemented by satellite based surveillance by European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). The Supplier of Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance shall overfly areas within the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment section 5) two times weekly. The flights shall take place both at day time and at night time and under all weather conditions of common occurrence in the respective areas. Flights will be scheduled by the Supplier. During the flights the Danish waters shall be monitored with the purpose of identifying prospective pollution. Monitoring shall be conducted by means of sensor equipment, which is capable of monitoring the water surface for oil spill etc. The sensor equipment must be made available by the Supplier. During the flights the Supplier shall collect evidence of any observed pollution, hereunder by photo and other documentation and by means of air-drop of oil spill sampling buoys, with the purpose of for example giving the Danish Authorities information to assess the measures to be taken in combating the pollution and providing evidence for further investigation and/or preliminary charges. Specifically the Supplier shall provide the following for airborne maritime pollution surveillance: — Flight system; — sensor equipment; — air crew and system operators necessary for operating flight system and sensor equipment. The Supplier must prior to commencement undertake extensive practical training of his air crew and system operators. The Supplier must ensure that the system operators are at all times duly qualified and trained to perform the task. The Supplier shall be available for participation in multinational operations on behalf of Denmark. The number of such operations is expected to be up to three per year. Participation in such operations is comparable to the flights as described above. The Supplier shall be available/stand by for the duration of these operations.

Tarkoituksenamme on korvata nykyjärjestelmä ohjelmistopalvelulla (SaaS), joka mahdollistaa prosessien kehittämisen ja turvaa laadullisesti vakaan toiminnan.
